question: Concretely, what is a gate checking — a script's exit code, a numeric threshold, or a human reading a report?
The language-head arm was added after the kill line fired on the same 201 crops — how do you rule out that split being cherry-picked once you saw the data?
You flip production yourself in this setup — on a real team, who gets that authority, and how many people would need it?
Who actually turns a persona's NOT verdict into a design change, and can that person decline what the persona is asking for?
Is '9 seconds, simulated' a usability number at all, or is it just an agent describing its own read of the screen?

Your live-lot accuracy is based on one tapper's own judgment across 87 lots with a confidence interval spanning roughly 53 to 75 percent — what stops that from being both measurer and grader of your own tool?
When you say the panel 'walked' the screens, does that mean it actually rendered and interacted with the live UI, or just reasoned over code and a static viewport?
Is 65% on live lots good enough to ship to real users, and what's the target number before you'd call this done?
How does a lane actually start — do you type a command that creates the worktree and branch, or is that scripted somewhere in the starter kit?
With forty-five possible forks for one bug, who decides which ones actually get run first?
What's actually in the unattended.md file — how do you set the end time, the caps, and get a morning report without building your own platform?
What's the actual first thing a product manager who doesn't run worktrees should do Monday morning?
How do you pick the kill-line number before the run — is that just your gut, or is there a rule for how strict to set it?
A hundred experiments in two weeks — was that one person working full time, or could a team hit that pace part-time?
What does 'reviewer one tier up' mean in practice — do you hardcode which model reviews which, or does the coordinator pick per task?
The persona panel said DONE but your own phone said no — what changed in your process so that gap doesn't happen again?
You showed four different top-3 numbers that don't agree, from 65 to 83 percent — how do you decide which one to report when someone asks 'is it better' outside a talk?
What actually stops an unattended overnight agent from merging a change that passes its gate but is wrong in a way the gate didn't anticipate?
What did the flapping actually look like to someone trying to use the scout, and did you watch a real person react to it before calling it fixed?
Are the four persona briefs built from real usability research, or are they demographics like '22, phone-only' dressed up as jobs?
The August bakeoff median of 10.4 seconds came from only six captures — how confident are you that number would hold up with a larger sample?
You call the 30-minutes-a-day figure your own estimate rather than a measurement — did you ever actually log your hours, and if not why present it alongside otherwise-instrumented numbers?
For the persona review gate, who writes the persona briefs and how does the agent 'walk' the build — screenshots, Playwright, something else?
Thirty minutes a day is your estimate and doesn't count morning review time — what's the real daily time cost end to end?
After the panel missed the fixed-viewport failure, did you change how the panel walks screens, or just add the human phone check on top?
The coordinator is your strongest model judging your own lanes — on a team, who plays that role, and can a junior PM own it?
What specifically changed on the review screen that cut your labeling verdict from three minutes to twenty seconds, and did anyone other than you time it?
When a usage limit killed three build lanes mid-work, what happened next — did you manually restart them, or is there a retry mechanism?
Who writes the kill bar before a run — you alone, or could someone else on a team set that gate?
Is the full experiment ledger and the replay data behind these charts public in the repo, or are some of these numbers from private logs I can't verify myself?
What is the language head, mechanically — a small classifier bolted onto the embedding output?
The persona panel said DONE on a fixed viewport but your own phone showed it was unusable — how many other DONE verdicts from that panel have you since re-checked on a real device?
For the live demo, was the card that held actually held long enough for a hand to tap it, or just long enough to look stable on stage?
Do the persona briefs ever get revised based on what real users actually do, or do they stay fixed once written?
Beyond the $9 in labeling calls, what does the Claude Max subscription itself cost, and does that scale if a whole team runs this?
Letting the swarm self-steer broke the next day and you had to keep correcting it — what exactly went wrong, and is that failure mode still possible today?
How do the lane branches actually merge back once a gate passes — do you squash-merge automatically, or is that a manual review step too?
What does replaying a recorded session offline actually involve — is that a custom tool, or something off the shelf?
Since one panel already returned a false DONE on a real device, how many other screens have you not yet re-checked by hand?
For the jitter fix, how do you attribute the drop between the 3x faster server and the cancel-but-keep-answer change beyond just not crediting one alone?
